This is a useful, community-minded approach and aligns with past OFBiz modernization efforts.

- Exposing OFBiz services as REST and consuming them with modern web/mobile stacks is a known pattern (Apache WINK + Angular/Material; mobile with Ionic/Cordova was demonstrated previously) — your PoC follows that approach [63406622-1].  
- OFBiz’s architecture is purposely loosely coupled and designed to be extended, and the Apache‑2.0 license makes iterative/custom changes practical without forcing you to publish proprietary changes — this supports a step‑by‑step, non-invasive modernization strategy (keeping core stock where possible) [7766061-2].  
- Real‑world user stories show the services do work and OFBiz is a solid platform to build on, but also warn that the out‑of‑the‑box UI is limited and the architecture/coding practices can be hard to grasp — so minimizing invasive core changes and providing clear documentation for a headless approach is prudent [6553967-3][6553967-10].  
- When packaging a plugin and demo setup, leverage OFBiz tools and conventions: webtools/entity engine, OFBiz-component.xml, demo vs seed data, and servicedef/entitydef — and include explicit README steps for loading demo data so others can reproduce your end‑to‑end demo [6553967-15].

In short: your direction is well-founded and likely to be broadly useful — keep the core stock, document the demo data & setup clearly, and surface the REST/service definitions so others can reuse and extend the PoC. References: [63406622-1] [7766061-2] [6553967-3] [6553967-10] [6553967-15].

Short answer: inventory is updated when the returned items are actually received/processed by the warehouse — not merely when the return record is marked complete/approved. Make sure the “receive” step has been done for the return (or update the return before receiving) [7471112-2][7471112-5][73634379-15][73634379-17].

What to check/do
- Check the per-item return response type (Wait and Replace / Replace Immediately / Refund and Replace Immediately) — these determine whether the system expects the original item back and how the return is handled [7471112-2][7471112-4][7471112-5].  
- Ensure the warehouse has processed the physical return and set the item status to “received” (company receives and processes the items). Inventory changes occur when the company/warehouse processes the returned items as received [7471112-2][7471112-5].  
- If you need to change quantities on an existing return before receipt, use the Update Return flow (add/remove items or edit returnable qty) and then complete the Receive Sales Return step so inventory updates [73634379-17][73634379-15].

If after confirming the receive step inventory still hasn’t changed, re-run the “receive”/process-return action or check logs/transactions for the return processing (the docs describe the receive/process step as the inventory-affecting action) [7471112-2][7471112-5].

Short answer — use the Demo & Test Setup Guide + the OFBiz Tutorial for current build/run instructions, and the gradle-wrapper is missing (so ./gradlew cannot find org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain) [7766066-3][7766066-2][184617942-4].

What to read first
- Demo and Test Setup Guide — Building OFBiz and Quick & Easy Setup (current recommended build/start instructions) [7766066-3][7766066-2].  
- OFBiz Tutorial — running/build examples and the exact gradlew startup commands (includes load-data examples) [184617942-4][170266058-41].

Why you get "Could not find or load main class org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain"
- That error means the Gradle wrapper classes (gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar and related wrapper files) are not present or the wrapper script cannot run. OFBiz expects you to use the embedded wrapper (run ./gradlew on *nix), or to initialize a wrapper if missing [7766066-3][170266058-41].

Immediate steps to fix
1. From your ofbiz directory run the wrapper-init command (creates/repairs wrapper files):
   ./gradlew init-gradle-wrapper
   (from OFBiz tutorial instructions) [170266058-41].  
2. Then run a clean build/start (examples):
   ./gradlew cleanAll
   ./gradlew "ofbiz --load-data readers=seed,seed-initial"
   or the combined form used in the tutorial: ./gradlew cleanAll loadAll ofbiz [170266058-41][184617942-4].  
3. Make sure you invoke the wrapper with ./gradlew (Linux/Unix/macOS) and that the script is executable; the docs require ./gradlew on *nix [7766066-3].  
4. If you prefer a system Gradle installation instead of the wrapper, that is possible though the docs treat it as out of scope — the wrapper is the recommended route [7766066-3].

Java version note
- For current OFBiz releases the Quick & Easy Setup requires Java 17 and that JAVA_HOME be set to that JDK; older tutorial pages reference JDK 8 for older releases — prefer Java 17 for recent installs [7766066-2][170266058-41].

About MySQL
- The provided docs describe using the embedded database (Derby or H2) for demo data; MySQL-specific configuration is not in these excerpts — you’ll need the MySQL datasource setup steps from the configuration docs (not included here) [7766066-2][184617942-4].

If you still see the same wrapper-class error after init-gradle-wrapper, say so and I’ll point to the exact wrapper files to check (gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties) and the next troubleshooting steps [170266058-41][7766066-3].

Short answer: update your OFBiz working copy with the SCM (svn up or git pull) and run the upgrade steps — do not need to re-clone every time. See below.

Steps (from OFBiz docs)
- Update your OFBiz home from the repository: svn up or git pull [7045166-0][13271445-2].
- Ensure your local/vendor branches are clean and up-to-date if you keep local customizations (vendor-branch workflow) [6554014-8].
- Run the upgrade/migration steps in the OFBiz home directory:
  - ./gradlew clean
  - ./gradlew "ofbiz --load-data readers=seed"
  - ./gradlew ofbiz
  (these let OFBiz apply automatic DB table/column changes; check the Revisions Requiring Data Migration page for any manual migration steps) [7045166-0].
- Note: releases are managed via branches (release<YY.MM>), so you may update to trunk or a release branch depending on which line you follow [48203381-8].

So: use svn up / git pull (or the vendor-branch update pattern) rather than routinely re-cloning. If you have local changes, keep them in your branch/vendor copy and make sure the base is clean before updating [6554014-8][7045166-0].

Short answer first:
- OFBiz’s Manufacturing app already includes Production Costing, Equipment Billing and Shipment Plans so costing and shipment are handled as part of the manufacturing flow; production runs (work orders) are the central point where materials, routing and costing come together [doc:applications/manufacturing/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/mfg-intro.adoc-0] [113708351-0] [340037431-0].
- For scrap/waste, use the product/BOM model: represent scrap or waste as a product (or intermediate product) and reflect it in BOMs/production runs so it can be tracked through MRP and reporting [doc:applications/manufacturing/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/mfg-intro.adoc-0] [6553827-6] [340037431-0].

Guidance and practical tips

1) Costing and shipment integration
- Recognize the built-in capabilities: OFBiz Manufacturing lists Production Costing and Equipment Billing as native features; Shipment Plans are a listed feature for handling outbound logistics [doc:applications/manufacturing/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/mfg-intro.adoc-0] [113708351-0].
- Use production runs (work orders) as the integration point: production runs tie BOMs, routing/tasks and produced quantities together — that is where costs and resource/equipment billing are attributed and where finished-goods movement can be coordinated with shipment plans [340037431-0] [doc:applications/manufacturing/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/mfg-intro.adoc-0].
- Before implementing, document your processes (materials, suppliers, triggers for manufacture and shipping) so you can map costing and shipment rules into OFBiz (planning, when to create shipments, what triggers costing entries) [113708351-10].

2) Handling scrap / waste material
- Model scrap explicitly in the product/BOM structure: OFBiz supports BOMs for intermediate and end products — you can represent scrap or waste as a product (or an intermediate component) and include it in BOMs or production-run records so quantities and cost impacts are tracked by MRP and costing [6553827-6] [doc:applications/manufacturing/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/mfg-intro.adoc-0] [340037431-0].
- Practical approach: define a “scrap” product(s) (or category) and record scrap quantities on the production run / BOM adjustments so the system captures material usage and enables reporting and costing analysis [340037431-0] [6553827-6].

References used
- Manufacturing & MRP feature list and Production Costing / Equipment Billing / Shipment Plans [doc:applications/manufacturing/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/mfg-intro.adoc-0] [113708351-0]
- Advice to model and document processes before configuration [113708351-10]
- Production run / work order and demo-data explanation (how BOMs, routing and production runs tie together) [340037431-0]
- BOM / production schema capabilities (intermediate/end products and integrated MRP) [6553827-6]

Short answer: the failure is caused by the accounting GL post (createAcctgTransAndEntries → postAcctgTrans) throwing an exception and forcing the transaction to rollback. Two documented workarounds:

1) If you don’t use the GL/accounting posting: comment out the secas_ledger entry in accounting/ofbiz-component.xml and restart the server (this prevents the failing accounting ECA from firing) [6553844-63].

2) If you want to keep accounting but avoid failing commits: either comment/disable the first <eca service="createAcctgTransAndEntries" event="commit"> rule in accounting/servicedef/secas_ledger.xml (it triggers postAcctgTrans), or configure an Error GL Journal so incomplete transactions are captured instead of failing the flow:
   - Create an error journal: Accounting → General Ledger → Setup → Journals.
   - Set it as “Error Gl Journal Id” in Accounting → General Ledger → Setup → Accounting Preferences.
   - View incomplete/unposted transactions at List Unposted Acctg Trans (Accounting → General Ledger → List Unposted Acctg Trans) [6553844-82].

Either approach requires restarting OFBiz after the config/xml change. These steps are the documented remedies for the “createAcctgTransAndEntries / transaction rollback / Current Location Stack” errors [6553844-63][6553844-82].

Short answer: QuickShip failed because OFBiz didn’t find any items that were both ready and available to be shipped. QuickShip only works when inventory is on‑hand, payment is acceptable, and no warehouse/third‑party steps are required. Check availability or create a shipment via the warehouse flow instead. [doc:applications/order/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/Help-order-view.adoc-4] [doc:applications/order/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/Help-order-view.adoc-6]

What to check and what to do
- Verify inventory on hand at the Facility for the ordered product (QOH > 0). If QOH is 0 (or ATP negative) the item isn’t available for QuickShip and must be produced/transferred first. [6553921-0]  
- Confirm payment/credit is acceptable (QuickShip presumes payment is OK). [doc:applications/order/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/Help-order-view.adoc-4]  
- If you intend to use the warehouse fulfillment path (not QuickShip), open the Order View and click the "New Shipment For Ship Group #[…]" link to generate a shipment. On that Facility Manager screen click Submit/Update so addresses and IDs are populated, set Ready/Ship/Receive dates and proceed through Scheduled → Picked → Packed → Shipped. [doc:applications/order/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/Help-order-view.adoc-6]  
- If you want to use Quick‑Ship, only use it once inventory is present and payment is confirmed; Quick‑Ship bypasses picking/packing but still requires items be on hand. After a successful Quick‑Ship the order status becomes Completed and a Shipment/Invoice will be created. [doc:applications/order/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/Help-order-view.adoc-4]

If after verifying inventory and payment you still see the same warning, use the warehouse shipment link to inspect the ship group and shipment details (addresses, dates, facility) and Submit/Update that shipment screen so the system can create the shipment record. [doc:applications/order/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/Help-order-view.adoc-6]

Short, practical guidance (based on the OFBiz docs you provided).

Key facts to keep in mind
- OFBiz is built with a loosely‑coupled architecture, unified data model and modular components — this makes components easier to understand, extend and migrate between releases [184617942-1][7766061-2][93325429-1].  
- OFBiz is Apache‑licensed (ASL2): you may modify and keep proprietary changes, but do not remove copyright/attribution notices in files [184617942-1][93325429-1][69406219-1].  
- The 18.12 tutorial is the relevant developer guide for the target release (also see 17.12 and earlier guides for background) — start there for release‑specific info [184617942-1][93325429-1][69406219-1].

Recommended high‑level upgrade approach
1. Read the 18.12 developer/tutorial material first to learn new/changed patterns and tooling for that release [184617942-1].  
2. Backup everything: full database dump + all customized code/configuration/assets from your current OFBiz v16 instance (production and dev). (This is standard practice aligned with maintaining customizations under the open model described in the docs.) [184617942-1][7766061-2].  
3. Create an isolated development/staging instance of OFBiz 18.12 (download releases from ofbiz.apache.org) and do not touch production while testing [25199300-0][184617942-1].  
4. Port/test customizations as separate extensions/modules where possible rather than patching core files — the architecture’s modularity and unified data model is designed to make this easier (this reduces merge conflicts with core changes) [184617942-1][7766061-2].  
5. Migrate or import data into the 18.12 test instance and validate business flows and reports thoroughly. Use iterative testing to identify API/data‑model changes that require mapping or transformation. The tutorials for the releases will help understand code/config organization [184617942-1][93325429-1].  
6. Keep all required copyright/attribution notices in files when moving/customizing code to the new release to comply with the ASL2 license [184617942-1][69406219-1].  
7. Use a staged rollout: once testing and QA are complete, schedule a production migration with full backups and a rollback plan. Continue to use a separate branch/repository for your customizations so future merges from upstream are easier [184617942-1][7766061-2].

Where to get help / next steps
- Start by reading the 18.12 tutorial and relevant release docs for details on code/layout/changes [184617942-1].  
- Download the release from the OFBiz download page and set up a dev instance for hands‑on testing [25199300-0].  
- Engage the OFBiz community (mailing lists/forums) if you hit issues — the project receives frequent user feedback and support contributions [184617942-1][7766061-2].

If you want, tell me:
- which customizations (components changed, custom entities, screen/template changes, custom services, patches to core) you have — I can then point to the most relevant parts of the 18.12 tutorial and suggest priority areas to test. [184617942-1][93325429-1]

What OFBiz configuration to change
- OFBiz datasources use inline-jdbc entries in framework/entity config (edit framework/entity/configentityengine.xml) — set the jdbc-uri there. Example inline-jdbc entries in the OFBiz docs show jdbc-uri like jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5433/ofbiz and other postgres examples you should replace with your ssl-enabled URI [71013152-20][71013152-11].

Make sure the JDBC driver is installed
- The docs show you must have the JDBC driver available for OFBiz; ensure the PostgreSQL JDBC jar is placed where OFBiz expects JDBC drivers (examples in the docs mention copying the JDBC driver jar for other DBs into entity/lib/jdbc) [71013152-16].

Limitations of the provided documentation
- The documentation excerpts provided here only show how to configure the inline-jdbc jdbc-uri and where JDBC drivers belong; they do not include any instructions for configuring Java keystore/truststore or presenting a client certificate to a PostgreSQL server. Because the server-side pg_hba entry you described (hostssl ... cert) requires the client to present a certificate, you will need steps beyond these excerpts to configure Java/driver client-cert usage (those steps are not present in the provided docs) [71013152-20][71013152-11][71013152-16].

References: inline-jdbc examples and jdbc-uri usage [71013152-20][71013152-11]; JDBC driver placement note [71013152-16].

Brief summary of the proposed fulfillment-api and what it already covers (so you can judge gaps against your merchants' needs):

- Purpose: a merchant-facing REST API for OFBiz-run WMS/3PLs to let merchants submit fulfillment orders, poll status & tracking, and request cancellations — built on the existing rest-api plugin and the stock OFBiz data model [430408954-0][430408954-1].

- Exposed endpoints (v1 proposal):
  - POST /rest/auth/token (JWT auth via rest-api)
  - GET /rest/fulfillment/stores — list stores granted to caller
  - POST /rest/fulfillment/stores/{productStoreId}/orders — create fulfillment order
  - GET /rest/fulfillment/stores/{productStoreId}/orders?modifiedSince=… — incremental status polling
  - GET /rest/fulfillment/stores/{productStoreId}/orders/{orderId} — full order detail incl. shipments + tracking
  - POST /rest/fulfillment/stores/{productStoreId}/orders/{orderId}/cancel — request cancellation
  [430408954-3]

- Key design principles that affect merchant requirements:
  - OFBiz-native contract (uses OFBiz field names and status ids) and no new tenancy entities — merchants are PartyGroup and accounts are ProductStore; access is via ProductStoreRole grants; idempotent intake via OrderHeader.externalId; per-store path scoping and grant validation for multi-merchant isolation [430408954-4][430408954-1].
  - Thin declarative REST over testable domain services; JWT auth and OpenAPI support; separation of mapping/validation/tenancy in services [430408954-4].
  - API-only (no UI/workflow changes); relies on existing stock/order model (Facilities, InventoryItem.ownerPartyId, Shipment + tracking) — no schema or framework changes; purely additive [430408954-1][430408954-6].

- Project-level benefits: establishes a reusable domain-API pattern (declarative resource files, tenancy-checked services, machine-readable error tokens, isolation tests) that other domain APIs can copy; makes "OFBiz as 3PL WMS" an out-of-the-box deployment story [430408954-6][430408954-0].

If you run or evaluated OFBiz for warehouse/3PL, please check whether the above covers your merchants' needs and tell us specifically:
- Do merchants need additional endpoints or webhook/callbacks instead of polling? (note: v1 proposes polling endpoints) [430408954-3]
- Any required fields, status semantics, or error contract expectations beyond raw OFBiz fields/status ids? (the API uses OFBiz-native naming and status ids) [430408954-4]
- Authentication/tenant-grant workflows or provisioning needs not covered by ProductStoreRole grants and JWT? [430408954-4]
- Any billing/financial, return-to-vendor, or advanced shipment/route management flows that must be exposed via API (these are not in the v1 endpoint list) [430408954-3]

This proposal is intentionally small, additive, and intended as a reference pattern for future APIs; your concrete merchant requirements will directly shape v1 and the pilot test scenarios [430408954-0][430408954-6].

(References: proposal abstract, scenario, endpoints, design principles, benefits) [430408954-0][430408954-1][430408954-3][430408954-4][430408954-6]

This can happen because invoicing/fulfillment and payment capture are separate steps in OFBiz:

- Invoices are created when the shipment is marked Packed; the system/Accountant sends the invoice and later associates received payments and marks invoices paid when money is actually received [7471143-0].  
- Credit-card authorization (which can auto-approve the order) is not the same as capture/receipt of funds; capture for CC payments is a separate action that (for CCs) is performed when shipment is Packed (automated capture) — otherwise payment must be received/associated by the Accountant before an invoice should be marked paid [7471159-1] [7471143-0].

So an invoice can be moved forward while the payment remains in an uncaptured/received state if capture hasn’t happened or if the invoice was advanced/marked manually before the payment was associated. Check whether the CC capture was performed at Packed time or whether the Accountant has associated a received payment with the invoice [7471143-0].
